title: Non-invasive hemodynamic and biomechanic imaging methods for early risk prediction in aortic dissection
text:
Aortic dissection (AD) is a potentially lethal disease, with chronic patients subjected to lifelong risks (such as
aortic growth, rupture and death) that require specialized care, lifelong follow up and potentially repeat
interventions. Current techniques for predicting risk in AD patients are limited and largely based on simple
anatomic measurements which do not capture the functional processes believed to play an important role
development of aortic growth and complications. Using a combination of state-of-the-art medical imaging
techniques, this project will deliver functional measures of aortic pressure and wall stiffness, enabling us to
shift the paradigm of patient assessment to provide timely, individualized medical and surgical care.

title: Targeting PTGIR-Prostacyclin Signaling to Overcome T Cell Exhaustion and Enhance Anti-Tumor Immunity
text:
I recently discovered a protein-lipid immune checkpoint that promotes tumor growth and immune dysfunction.
Here, I will determine how cancer cells exploit this checkpoint to evade the host immune system, and
demonstrate that blocking this checkpoint can revitalize immune cells to better control cancer.

title: Novel molecular mechanisms of vascular smooth muscle cell-mediated large and small artery calcification
text:
The discovery of new and effective treatments for cardiovascular diseases requires the identification of novel
disease mechanisms. This proposal aims to enhance our mechanistic insights of vascular calcification by
focusing on the activation of autophagy pathway to prevent the development of artery calcification in humans.
Success in identifying the specific molecules in this pathway implicated in the development of calcification will
provide new targets for treatment of peripheral arterial disease.

title: A cross protective multivalent vaccine for Shigella and ETEC
text:
This project combines the expertise of Johns Hopkins University and the University of Illinois at Urbana-
Champaign to develop a safe and broadly protective combination vaccine against enterotoxigenic Escherichia
coli (ETEC) and Shigella, two leading causes of children’s diarrhea and travelers’ diarrhea. Currently, there is
no licensed vaccine for either ETEC or Shigella, but the novel epitope- and structure- based MEFA (multiepitope
fusion antigen) vaccinology platform together with appropriate animal challenge models make feasible the
development and evaluation of a safe and broadly protective multivalent combination vaccine for ETEC and
Shigella. An effective ETEC-Shigella vaccine will have a major beneficial impact on children’s health, and this
MEFA technology may be applied generally for safe and precision multivalent vaccine development.

title: Deconstructing human body plan development with stem cells
text:
Understanding human body plan development will shine light on the etiology of congenital diseases and
contribute to regenerative medicine. I have established in vitro models of human somite formation using
pluripotent stem cells and will construct novel models recapitulating human limb development. Building on my
finding that cell sorting underlies somite anteroposterior patterning, I will continue using these models to
illuminate mechanisms of pattern formation along the body axis and appendages.

title: IBD Gene Mapping by Clinical and Population Subset
text:
According to the Center for Disease Control and Prevention, an estimated 1.4 million Americans suffer from
Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD), a chronic debilitating disorder that includes Crohn’s disease and ulcerative
colitis. IBD ranks in the top 5 in prevalence for gastrointestinal disorders and represents a significant financial
burden to society requiring a lifetime of medical care as there is no cure for this disease. This proposed
research aims to determine the genetic variations that cause IBD which will aid in developing preventive
measures, improving the quality of care with better treatment plans and educating patients through genetic
counseling.

title: Causes and Downstream Effects of 14-3-3 Phosphorylation in Synucleinopathies
text:
14-3-3 proteins play a role in many different cellular functions, diseases, and pathologies through the hundreds
of protein networks they interact with. We have already shown 14-3-3 proteins are protective in models of
synucleinopathies such as Parkinson’s Disease and Dementia with Lewy Bodies while phosphorylation of 14-
3-3 is detrimental to this protection. Our goal is to understand what causes this phosphorylation and how that
phosphorylation changes the protein networks 14-3-3s interact with to discover new therapeutic targets for
these disorders.

title: Neutralization of primary HIV-1 viruses
text:
The proposed research seeks knowledge that will inform effective strategies for a vaccine that protects against
HIV-1 by inducing broadly active neutralizing antibodies, and for using such antibodies optimally to treat infection.
The research is therefore relevant to public health because, according to UNAIDS, as of 2021 38 million people
were living with HIV, of whom 10 million lacked access to antiretroviral therapy, while 1.5 million people became
newly infected with the virus and 650,000 died from AIDS and related illnesses that year. The application focuses
on the molecular basis of the binding by neutralizing antibodies in relation to their breadth and efficacy of action,
aiming to inform not only vaccine development but also the use of neutralizing antibodies to treat or prevent
infection.

title: Dissecting Convergent Somatic and Germline Alterations that Mediate the Origins and Evolution of Kidney Cancer
text: Both somatic and germline events contribute to clear cell renal cell carcinoma pathogenesis, though biological convergence between these events to promote this disease are incompletely understood. Through integrative and hypothesis-driven computational, functional, and clinical approaches, we will dissect the convergent regulatory processes that arise from somatic-germline interactions in kidney cancer to yield novel and translatable biological discoveries.

title: Beyond Binding: Personalized Multi-omic Neoantigen Identification
text:
This project aims to improve cancer treatment by developing laboratory tests and advanced
software that can accurately predict which cancer-specific markers, known as neoantigens,
are likely to activate the immune system. By integrating detailed genetic information from
cancer patients, the technology will help customize immunotherapy treatments to be more
effective. This research could lead to better, more personalized therapies that target cancer
cells without harming normal cells, potentially improving survival and quality of life for cancer
patients.

title: Elucidating SPEN-Driven m6A Regulation During Henipavirus Infection
text:
Henipaviruses are emerging, highly lethal BSL-4 RNA viruses with poorly characterized
mechanisms of pathogenesis. This research will elucidate how henipaviruses manipulate m6A
regulatory pathways to enhance infection, using a novel surrogate system combined with
biochemical, virological, and high-throughput transcriptomic approaches. Through this work, I
will gain advanced training in molecular virology, host-pathogen interactions, and multi-omic
analysis under expert mentorship, preparing me for a career as an independent research
scientist.

title: Mechanisms of Interoceptive Signaling in Mouse Colon
text:
Interoception, the sensing of internal bodily states, plays a crucial role in both physical and emotional
well-being. This proposal seeks to uncover specific neural circuits linking the spinal cord dorsal horn
and brainstem that are uniquely involved in processing visceral interoceptive signals from the colon.
The goal is to identify novel therapeutic targets for the treatment of disorders rooted in dysfunctional
visceral interoception.

title: Modeling the Effect of Apolipoprotein LI Risk Variants on CVD Risk in African American E-cigarette Users Using Human Induced Pluripotent Stem-Cell-Derived Endothelial Cells
text:
African American individuals are more likely to die from tobacco-related cardiovascular diseases compared to
other races; nevertheless, their representation in research is limited. By leveraging a robust platform for modeling
cardiovascular risk, induced pluripotent stem cell derived endothelial cells (iPSC-ECs), the proposed research
aims to investigate the influence of highly prevalent genetic markers, specific to this demographic and extremely
rare in other racial groups, on vascular health among traditional cigarette and e-cigarette users. This project will
provide crucial information about the vascular health effects of these most commonly used tobacco products,
while identifying molecular targets to guide precise interventions and address health disparities within the high-
risk African American population.

title: The genomic and epigenomic landscape of otosclerosis
text:
This proposal leverages genomic and epigenomic techniques in an assembled large cohort of families and
unrelated cases to unravel the molecular etiology of otosclerosis, an age-related disorder characterized by an
abnormal bone remodeling in the otic capsule. Findings from this study may aid in risk prediction, screening,
patient management and treatment.

title: Elucidating ATP8B1 Deficiency Using Genetic Modifiable Patient-Derived iPSC-livers
text:
This project will use patient-specific iPS cells to investigate how ATP8B1 deficiency, previously known as PFIC1, disrupts
bile acid metabolism and triggers adaptive stress responses in liver cells. Understanding these mechanisms will provide
critical insights to guide the development of new therapeutic strategies for patients with ATP8B1 deficiency and related liver
diseases.

title: Mechanistic roles of bitter taste receptors in the pathogenesis and treatment of chronic rhinosinusitis
text:
Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is a widespread and costly airway disease characterized by persistent inflammation
and infection that often fails to respond to current medical and surgical therapies. This project will define how
bitter taste receptors (TAS2Rs) in nasal ciliated and tuft cells regulate host defense and inflammation by using
newly developed mouse models that either lack endogenous Tas2r genes or are humanized with specific human
TAS2R genes, and will test these models using in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo systems. The results will identify
distinct TAS2R-mediated mechanisms that can be leveraged to develop novel and effective therapies for CRS
and related airway diseases.

title: Deciphering the Transcriptional Regulatory Network Controlling RGC Axon Growth to Promote RGC Axon Regeneration and Cell Survival after Axonal Injury
text:
Understanding the complex gene regulatory network controlling axon growth is a critical step to meet the
challenge of poor axon regeneration in the central nervous system. The proposed study will combine RNA-seq
and ATAC-seq in purified retinal ganglion cells at various developmental stages and use advanced integrative
multi-omics analysis to identify core transcription factors regulating axon growth during retinal ganglion cell
development, and functionally test the identified transcription factors in optic nerve regeneration model. The
study will not only provide a comprehensive view of the transcriptional regulatory network that governs neuronal
axon growth, but also reveal novel therapeutic targets for glaucoma and other neural injuries and
neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Estradiol-mediated Gene Signatures in Hippocampal Memory
text:
This proposal will provide insight into how the potent sex-steroid hormone 17-estradiol (E2) controls
gene expression programs in a cell-type specific manner in the hippocampus, a brain region important
for learning and memory whose function is compromised during aging and in certain mental health
disorders. The proposed research is relevant to public health because it will improve our understanding
of the neurobiological underpinnings that support healthy cognitive function, and inform the
development of sex-specific therapeutic intervention strategies to treat neuropsychiatric disorders
influenced by the hormonal milieu. Moreover, this work is particularly relevant to the NIMH’s first
Strategic Objective (Strategy 1.1) which seeks to define cellular and molecular gene regulatory
mechanisms relevant to cognitive function and mental health.

title: High-throughput Functional Analysis of Autism Risk Genes
text:
There is an urgent need to advance from the discovery of genes that are strongly associated with autism
spectrum disorders (ASDs) to the identification of basic biological mechanisms as a path to discover new
therapeutic targets. We propose to use an innovative, high-throughput approach to investigate the function of
multiple ASD genes in parallel in the developing brain. Our central goal is to identify novel pathways downstream
of ASD genes and pharmacological targets for further investigation.

title: Characterizing and therapeutically targeting pH-regulatory mechanisms in the perivascular and infiltrating niches of glioblastoma using amine CEST-EPI and a novel treatment platform
text:
Glioblastoma continues to exhibit extremely poor survival despite novel therapies. We hypothesize that a major
contributor to this treatment failure is lack of attention to non-enhancing infiltrative tumor cells. The proposed
research will explore novel pH based visualization and modulation of these infiltrative tumor cells with the goal
of surgical and molecular targeting these progenitors of recurrence.
